## Natural history notes

A very small erebid moth characterized by narrow brown to tan wings, subtle darker mottling, and a delicate resting posture typical of small owlet-like moths in the Noctuoidea. In Florida, Proroblemma testa has been recorded from sites including Collier-Seminole State Park near Naples and appears on Florida moth lists, so it is best treated as a warm-climate moth of wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats where adults may come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it should be described cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed concealed on foliage or low vegetation while supporting bats, birds, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
